    assert sort_array([1, 5, 2, 3, 4]) == [1, 2, 4, 3, 5]

def test_sort_array():
    # Empty array
    assert sort_array([]) == []

    # Single element
    assert sort_array([1]) == [1]
    assert sort_array([0]) == [0]

    # Basic case: sorted by number of 1s in binary, ties broken by value
    # 1->'1'(1), 2->'10'(1), 3->'11'(2), 4->'100'(1), 5->'101'(2)
    assert sort_array([1, 5, 2, 3, 4]) == [1, 2, 4, 3, 5]

    # Consecutive values 0-7
    # ones: 0->0, 1->1, 2->1, 3->2, 4->1, 5->2, 6->2, 7->3
    assert sort_array([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]) == [0, 1, 2, 4, 3, 5, 6, 7]

    # Negative numbers: bin(-n)[2:] counts ones in magnitude
    # -2->'10'(1), -3->'11'(2), -4->'100'(1), -5->'101'(2), -6->'110'(2)
    assert sort_array([-2, -3, -4, -5, -6]) == [-4, -2, -6, -5, -3]

    # Duplicates
    assert sort_array([3, 3, 1]) == [1, 3, 3]
    assert sort_array([5, 5, 5]) == [5, 5, 5]

    # Powers of two (single bit set) keep numeric order
    assert sort_array([8, 16, 15]) == [8, 16, 15]
    assert sort_array([2, 4, 8]) == [2, 4, 8]

    # Mixed with zero (zero has zero ones, sorts first)
    assert sort_array([7, 0, 5]) == [0, 5, 7]

    # Larger numbers
    # 1023->'1111111111'(10), 256->'100000000'(1), 255->'11111111'(8)
    assert sort_array([1023, 256, 255]) == [256, 255, 1023]

    # Already sorted input
    assert sort_array([1, 2, 4, 8]) == [1, 2, 4, 8]

    # Result is a list
    assert isinstance(sort_array([3, 1, 2]), list)

    print("All sort_array tests passed!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_sort_array()
